gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's maker-store prices for the small stations or what an hour of router backup costs on each. At EcoFlow's US store the 768 Wh RIVER 2 Pro is $369 today, only $79 more than the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2's $289.99, and it runs a 20 W router and modem for about 32.6 h instead of about 12.2 h ($11.3 vs $23.7 per hour of backup). Both Jackery 240 v2 and 300 v2 units are out of stock at Jackery.
standout_why: I compared against all three cited rival pages. homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/wifi-router-modem has undated list prices that are now out of date: RIVER 2 Pro $529 (EcoFlow charges $369 today), RIVER 2 Max $299 and Jackery Explorer 300 $289. It also leaves out the Elite 30 V2, Tenergy T320, ALLPOWERS R600 and Jackery 240 v2. outagemath.com/appliances/wifi-router and backupcalc.com/guides/how-long-will-a-power-station-run-a-wifi-router show no prices at all and no per-model switchover. None of the three gives stock status or cost per hour of backup. The two ChatGPT chats showed one price each, $254.29 for the RIVER 3 and $269 at Best Buy for the Explorer 300 v2, both without dates.
decides: The finding confirms the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 ($289.99, in stock, ≤10 ms UPS by BLUETTI's spec) as the pick for a small, seamless backup. Of the ~300 Wh models I priced today, it's the only one in stock that is also published at ≤10 ms. Jackery's 300 v2 matches it on paper (≤0.01 s) but is sold out on jackery.com. The finding adds two side picks. For the longest runtime per dollar, the RIVER 2 Pro (768 Wh, $369, <30 ms EPS, 18.2 lb) covers a full day plus a night. For the lowest price, the Tenergy T320 ($225.99) runs a 12 V router from DC barrel ports, but Tenergy publishes no switchover, so the router may reboot when the power drops.

findings.note: Read from the Shopify product JSON. No strikethrough price (compare_at equals price), available: true. The listing says ≤10 ms UPS and 4.5 W standby. Kits with a 60 W panel cost $399.99 and with a 100 W panel $489.99. At 20 W: 288 Wh × 0.85 / 20 W = 12.2 h, so $289.99 / 12.2 h = $23.7 per hour of backup. The 85% factor is the AC efficiency that backupcalc.com and ChatGPT both use; standby draw is not included.
